subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence with correct subject–verb agreement.
options: Neither the manager nor the employees know the schedule.
Neither the manager nor the employees knows the schedule.
Neither the managers nor the employee know the schedule.
Neither the manager nor the employees is responsible for the schedule.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearest subject. 'Employees' (plural) requires 'know', so option 2 is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: "By the time she arrived, we ___ dinner."
explanation: Use past perfect for an action completed before another past action: 'had finished' (past perfect) is required.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym: "He was reluctant to accept the award."
explanation: 'Reluctant' means 'unwilling' or hesitant. 'Eager' and 'pleased' mean the opposite; 'proud' is different in meaning.

subject: English Language
text: What does 'bit the bullet' mean in: "After months of delay, she bit the bullet and signed the contract."
options: She avoided the decision at last.
She accepted an unpleasant action and endured it.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept and endure something unpleasant; it denotes facing a difficult necessity, so option 2 fits.

subject: English Language
text: Which option correctly punctuates and capitalises this sentence? "mrs adeyemi who teaches mathematics will retire in June"
options: Mrs. Adeyemi, who teaches mathematics, will retire in June.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Non-restrictive clause needs commas and proper capitals: 'Mrs. Adeyemi, who teaches mathematics, will retire in June.' is correctly punctuated and capitalised.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: balloon, garden, music, little?
explanation: 'balloon' is pronounced ba-LOON with primary stress on the second syllable; the others have stress on their first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: bat, bad, bee, bag?
explanation: 'Bee' has the long /iː/ vowel; 'bat', 'bad' and 'bag' have the short /æ/ vowel, so 'bee' is phonetically different.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: "The committee will announce the results tomorrow."
options: Tomorrow, will announce the results by the committee.
The results will announce the committee tomorrow.
The committee will be announced the results tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
explanation: Form passive with object as subject + auxiliary + past participle: 'The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Fill the blank: "If he ___ earlier, he would have caught the bus."
explanation: Third conditional for a past unreal condition uses past perfect in the 'if' clause: 'If he had left earlier, he would have caught the bus.'

subject: English Language
text: Read: "Amaka watered the garden every evening. The vegetables flourished." What is the best inference?
options: She neglected the garden and the plants died.
Regular care helped the plants to grow well.
explanation: The passage links Amaka's regular evening watering with flourishing vegetables; the reasonable inference is that regular care helped them grow.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready for the test.'
explanation: Rule: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the noun nearest it. 'students' is plural, so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: Complete: 'By six o'clock he ___ his homework.'
explanation: Future perfect is used for an action completed before a specified future time: 'will have finished' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Read: 'After the sudden shower, Kemi dried the chair and left the umbrella on the balcony. The sun broke through the clouds.' What is the best inference?
explanation: Inference: drying and putting the umbrella away while the sun appears indicate the shower had ended; the rain stopped.

subject: English Language
text: What does the idiom mean: 'She kept her cards close to her chest.'
options: She was secretive about her plans.
She guarded a physical chest of cards.
explanation: Idiom explanation: 'keep one's cards close to one's chest' means to be secretive or to withhold information, not to share.

subject: English Language
text: Which option correctly punctuates and capitalises this sentence? 'professor okoro said the meeting starts at 9am'
options: Professor Okoro said the meeting starts at 9am.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
Professor Okoro said, 'The meeting starts at 9 a.m.'
A different grammatical construction is required
explanation: Correct form: capitalise the title and name, use a comma before a quotation, enclose speech in quotes, and write '9 a.m.' with periods.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: arrival, balance, photograph, market?
explanation: Pronunciation rule: 'arrival' is pronounced ə-RIVE-al with primary stress on the second syllable; the others have first-syllable stress.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound: cot, caught, cost, coat?
explanation: Phonetic contrast: 'coat' contains a diphthong /oʊ/ different from the open back vowel quality in cot/caught/cost.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most appropriate reply to: 'Why are you leaving early?'
options: Because I have a doctor's appointment.
explanation: Speech function: The question asks for a reason; only the first option provides an appropriate explanation of why someone is leaving.

subject: English Language
text: Change to indirect speech: Tunde said, 'I will call you tomorrow morning.'
options: Tunde said he will call me tomorrow morning.
Tunde said he calls you the next morning.
Tunde said he would call me the next morning.
Tunde said he had called you tomorrow morning.
explanation: Reported-speech rule: 'will' backshifts to 'would' and 'tomorrow morning' becomes 'the next morning'; pronoun 'you' becomes 'me'.

subject: English Language
text: Fill the blank: 'If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be postponed.'
explanation: First conditional structure: use present simple in the 'if' clause and future in the main clause. 'If it rains' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: "Each of the students ___ a locker."
explanation: Rule: 'each' with a plural-looking noun makes the noun phrase singular; use singular verb 'has' not plural 'have' or plural passive forms.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: "By 8 p.m. last night, Chinedu ___ his report."
explanation: Use past perfect ('had finished') for an action completed before a specific past time; simple past or present perfect do not express the same sequence.

subject: English Language
text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'skeptical'?
explanation: 'Skeptical' means doubtful or unbelieving; contrast: 'eager' (keen), 'certain' (sure), and 'admiring' (respectful) are not synonyms.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence: "After weeks of secrecy, he finally spilled the beans." What does "spilled the beans" mean here?
explanation: Idiom rule: 'spill the beans' means to reveal secret information; the other options are literal or opposite actions and do not match the idiom.

subject: English Language
text: Punctuate and capitalise this sentence correctly: "after lunch the teachers returned to the staffroom"
options: After lunch, the teachers returned to the staffroom.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Rule: introductory adverbial phrase 'After lunch' is followed by a comma; sentence must begin with a capital letter. Option with comma after phrase is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: control, yellow, teacher, dinner?
explanation: Stress pattern: con-TROL (second syllable stressed). 'Yellow', 'teacher' and 'dinner' have stress on the first syllable, so 'control' is the only second-syllable-stressed word.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: ship, chip, slip, sheep?
explanation: Phoneme contrast: 'ship', 'chip', 'slip' have the short vowel /ɪ/; 'sheep' has the long vowel /iː/, so 'sheep' differs in vowel quality.

subject: English Language
text: Your neighbour asks, "Would you mind feeding my cat while I'm away?" Which reply is most appropriate?
explanation: Pragmatic rule: 'Would you mind...?' is a polite request; an appropriate polite acceptance is 'Sure, I'd be happy to.' Other options are refusal, irrelevant, or rude.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: "Someone has stolen my bicycle."
explanation: Grammar: active present perfect 'has stolen' converts to present perfect passive 'has been stolen.' Simple past or past perfect choices do not match the original aspect.

subject: English Language
text: Read: "Rao left embers from his stove on the floor overnight. At dawn the embers spread and a small fire began; neighbours brought water to help." What is the best inference?
options: Rao was careless with the embers.
explanation: Inference: the sequence (left embers, embers spread, fire started) supports careless handling. Other options are not supported by the described events.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: 'A pair of scissors ___ on the table.'
explanation: The phrase 'a pair of' is treated as a singular subject; verb agrees as singular: 'a pair of scissors is'. This contrasts with plural verbs like 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: 'By the time the play started, Lily and Jonah ___ to their seats.'
explanation: Use past perfect ('had gone') for an action completed before another past event (the play starting); other options do not mark the earlier completed action correctly.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'meticulous' in: 'The tailor was meticulous about every stitch.'
explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise; 'precise' is the correct synonym. 'Careless', 'hasty' and 'vague' are antonyms and therefore incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: What does 'keep your nose to the grindstone' mean in: 'During the term, Musa kept his nose to the grindstone and studied without breaks.'
explanation: The idiom means to work hard and steadily; in context it means Musa worked diligently without breaks. The other options do not match the idiomatic meaning.

subject: English Language
text: Which option correctly punctuates and capitalises this sentence? 'last tuesday mrs. adu and mr. owusu visited the art gallery in accra'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Last Tuesday Mrs. Adu and Mr. Owusu visited the art gallery in Accra.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Days, titles and proper nouns must be capitalised and abbreviations punctuated: 'Last Tuesday Mrs. Adu and Mr. Owusu visited the art gallery in Accra.' Other options fail in capitals or punctuation.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: hotel, market, history, family?
explanation: 'Hotel' is pronounced ho-TEL with primary stress on the second syllable. 'Market', 'history' and 'family' have primary stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: beat, seat, great, heat?
explanation: 'Beat', 'seat' and 'heat' have the long /iː/ vowel, while 'great' has a diphthong /eɪ/; 'great' therefore has a different vowel sound.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most supportive reply to: 'I scored only 45% on the exam.'
explanation: A supportive reply acknowledges effort and encourages: 'At least you tried.' Other replies are unsupportive, sarcastic, or inappropriate to the speaker's disappointment.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive voice: 'They will publish the announcement next Monday.'
options: The announcement will publish next Monday.
Next Monday the announcement will publish by them.
The announcement will be published next Monday.
The announcement is published next Monday.
explanation: Passive of 'will publish' is formed with 'will be' + past participle: 'will be published'. Options with 'will publish' or present forms are incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: Amina closed the market stall earlier than usual and carried a heavy bag to her bicycle. The street was almost empty. What is the best inference from these sentences?
options: Amina was saving time by leaving early.
The market had been unusually crowded all day.
Amina likely planned to travel to another town tonight.
The area becomes quiet after the market closes, so few people remained.
explanation: Best inference: the empty street after she closed suggests the area is quiet once the market is closed. Other options are not directly supported by the given details.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the increase in taxes nor the proposed policy ___ popular with voters.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer noun; 'policy' is singular so use 'is'.

subject: English Language
text: Before the lights went out, the students ___ notes for an hour.
explanation: Use past perfect continuous 'had been taking' to show an action continuing up to a past point (lights going out).

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'frugal' as used: 'Mrs. Ebo is frugal with household spending.'
explanation: 'Frugal' means economical or sparing in expenditure; 'economical' matches meaning, others contrast by excess or neglect.

subject: English Language
text: What does 'bent over backwards' mean in: 'When customers complained, the shopkeeper bent over backwards to help.'
explanation: 'Bent over backwards' is an idiom meaning to make a great effort to help or accommodate someone.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised sentence: 'professor ntia announced the results would be released on monday'
options: Professor Ntia announced the results would be released on Monday.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals for titles and names and for days: 'Professor Ntia' and 'Monday' are correctly capitalised; punctuation is otherwise unchanged.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the second syllable: balance, decide, market, family?
explanation: 'Decide' has primary stress on the second syllable (de-CIDE). The other words have stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: ship, clip, grin, sheep?
explanation: 'Sheep' has the long /iː/ vowel, while 'ship', 'clip', and 'grin' use the short /ɪ/ vowel; so 'sheep' differs.

subject: English Language
text: Which reply is most appropriate to: 'Would you mind opening the window?'
options: Not at all, I'll open it.
explanation: Polite request 'Would you mind...' expects a polite offer or permission; 'Not at all, I'll open it.' accepts and offers to act.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive voice: 'Someone will finish the painting tomorrow.'
options: The painting will be finished tomorrow.
Tomorrow will be finished the painting by someone.
Someone will be finished with the painting tomorrow.
explanation: Passive moves object to subject and uses appropriate auxiliary: 'The painting will be finished tomorrow.' is correct passive form.

subject: English Language
text: Fill the blank: 'If he ___ the invitation, he would have met her.'
explanation: Third conditional: unreal past uses 'If + past perfect' (had accepted) with 'would have' to show hypothetical past result.
